nodes.name: New Task Form Submission
nodes.notes: Serves an n8n-hosted form (Title, Assignee, Duedate). Each submission becomes one execution.

nodes.name: Stamp & Shape Task
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes taskId, receivedAt. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Payload Valid?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.taskId }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Record Rejected Input
nodes.notes: Creates a new page in the Notion database — the title is pulled straight from the item's key field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Notion integration token. notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.

nodes.name: Prepare Approval Packet
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes requestId, summary, requestedBy. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Request Approval via Slack
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#projects) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Hold for Decision
nodes.notes: Pauses the execution until the resume webhook is called — this is the approval/HITL gate. Watch out: Long waits survive restarts, but the resume URL is single-use.

nodes.name: Approved?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.body?.decision || $json.decision }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Execute Approved Action (API)
nodes.notes: POST https://api.example.com/v1/tasks — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Record Decline + Notify Requester
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#projects) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Join Decision Paths
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Pulls every page from the Notion database — fine for small datasets; add a filter if the database grows large. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Notion integration token. notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.

nodes.name: Compute Drift vs Snapshot
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Compare current metrics with the previous snapshot Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per task (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.name: Archive Row Snapshot
nodes.notes: Creates a new page in the Notion database — the title is pulled straight from the item's key field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Notion integration token. notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.

nodes.name: Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
nodes.notes: Delegates to a reusable sub-workflow (single-responsibility building block) and waits for its result. Watch out: The sub-workflow needs an Execute Sub-workflow Trigger as its entry point. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Record Sub-workflow Result
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Enrich with Reference Data
nodes.notes: GET https://enrichment.example.com/v2/lookup — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Fold In Enrichment Fields
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes enrichedAt, enrichmentSource. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time
nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 100 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Align Field Names
nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

nodes.name: Save Execution Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Append Audit Row (MySQL)
nodes.notes: Inserts a row into the MySQL table using fields auto-mapped from the incoming item. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

nodes.notes: Posts to a Discord channel via an incoming webhook — no bot token needed, the webhook URL on the credential is the only secret. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Discord webhook URL. Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.

nodes.name: Capture Failure Context
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes failedNode, errorMessage, workflow. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.notes: Posts to a Discord channel via an incoming webhook — no bot token needed, the webhook URL on the credential is the only secret. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Discord webhook URL. Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.

nodes.name: Park in Dead-Letter Queue
nodes.notes: Inserts a row into the MySQL table using fields auto-mapped from the incoming item. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

# Approve requests with Notion

**Pattern:** Approval Workflow · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers onboarding work end to end across Notion, Slack, MySQL and Discord.

It moves through 29 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Task Form Submission
2. Stamp & Shape Task
3. Payload Valid?
4. Record Rejected Input
5. Prepare Approval Packet
6. Request Approval via Slack
7. Hold for Decision
8. Approved?
9. Execute Approved Action (API)
10. Record Decline + Notify Requester
11. Join Decision Paths
12. Load Previous Snapshot
13. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
14. Fingerprint for Idempotency
15. Drop Already-Processed Items
16. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
17. Archive Row Snapshot
18. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
19. Record Sub-workflow Result
20. Enrich with Reference Data
21. Fold In Enrichment Fields
22. Stamp Completion Time
23. Persist Run Metadata
24. Cap Batch Volume
25. Align Field Names
26. Save Execution Metadata
27. Summarize Run Stats
28. Append Audit Row (MySQL)
29. Send Summary to Discord

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing onboarding work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Task Form Submission → Stamp & Shape Task → Payload Valid? → Record Rejected Input → Prepare Approval Packet → Request Approval via Slack → Hold for Decision → Approved? → Execute Approved Action (API) → Record Decline + Notify Requester → Join Decision Paths → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Cap Batch Volume → Align Field Names → Save Execution Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (MySQL) → Send Summary to Discord → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Notion and Slack aligned by hand for onboarding
- Onboarding sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before Notion
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in Notion, for onboarding
- Onboarding work where "Stamp & Shape Task" is still a manual step before Notion

## You get

- Keeps Notion and Slack in step for onboarding, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Notion or Slack are skipped, across all 32 nodes of this onboarding build
- A failed Notion or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 32 nodes in this onboarding build
- Branches rejoin before Notion, so a onboarding run reports once rather than 32 times
- The pause before Notion is durable — a onboarding run survives a restart

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Discord webhook URL; MySQL connection; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The workflow pauses on a Wait node configured to resume via webhook — n8n's actual human-in-the-loop primitive, not a polling loop. The resume URL is embedded directly in the approval message so approving is one click, and the paused execution burns no compute for however long the decision takes.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Add a timeout to the Wait node so unanswered approvals auto-decline after N hours.
2. Change the approval channel and confirm the resume link still works.
3. Add a third outcome (e.g. 'needs changes') alongside approve/decline.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**MySQL connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.
_Gotcha:_ Remote access often needs the n8n server's IP allow-listed.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🙋 Human in the loop

The workflow pauses at the Wait node until a human posts a decision to the resume URL (included in the approval message). Approve → the action executes; anything else → recorded as declined. No timeout is set by default — add one under the Wait node's options if approvals go stale.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your onboarding process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- MySQL: grant the user only the tables this workflow touches; avoid `GRANT ALL` on the schema.
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole onboarding payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
